title: Amazon: attackers used the Cairn AI tool to exploit a MONAI Label zero-day and take over a server, BleepingComputer reports
date_note: Date of BleepingComputer's report; it says the attacks ran 8 to 10 September 2026 and the maintainers released a security update on 18 November.
org: East Asian educational institutions (MONAI Label users)
geo_basis: region named by the source: mainly East Asian educational institutions outside China; no pin for a single organisation
summary: BleepingComputer reports Amazon found AI agents running the Cairn tool exploiting a path traversal zero-day in MONAI Label, a medical imaging application, within 11 minutes of mapping its API. They gained root on a server; the operator then gave them a proxy into a second university network running the same software. Amazon attributes it to a Chinese-nexus actor with moderate confidence. A security update came on 18 November.
plain: Amazon says attackers used an autonomous AI tool to find and exploit a flaw in medical imaging software and take over a university server. A fix was released on 18 November.
exec: AI agents were reported to go from mapping an API to exploiting a flaw in 11 minutes; organisations running MONAI Label should apply the update.
action: If you run MONAI Label, apply the maintainers' security update (advisory GHSA-qc22-rmgc-vg94).

attribution.note: moderate confidence, from prompt language, activity timestamps and target choice, as relayed by BleepingComputer

validation.note: BleepingComputer and The Record (independent publishers) both relay Amazon's finding of a path traversal zero-day in a medical imaging application, used against a university and then a second one, since fixed by the maintainers. The Record does not name MONAI Label or give a confidence level; both rely on Amazon, whose own report was not read.

review.note: Softened reached second network to operator-provided proxy; added 11-minute figure to summary; removed unsourced authentication advice from action. Dates, attribution, patch date match BleepingComputer.
